newsitem.title: CHINA: Pudong to end duty-free imports for foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: Pudong to end duty-free imports for foreign firms.

text.p: Shanghai's Pudong development zone will completely abolish preferential policies on imports of equipment by the end of next year, the official Xinhua news agency said on Monday.

Foreign-invested firms in the zone have been allowed to import equipment and raw materials for self-use tax free or at reduced tariff rates, but the benefits have been scrapped for firms established after April 1.
The preferential policies will cease at the end of this year for firms with a total investment of less than $30 million, and for all companies at the end of next year, Xinhua said.

An official with the Pudong New Area Administrative Commission could not confirm details but said the abolition of prefential tax policies was a must for China in terms of its application to join the World Trade Organisation.
The preferential policies were adopted in the early 1990s when Beijing started to open Pudong to the outside world and was anxious to attract more foreign investment.
